<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa1fb6f4e0b162f768c340ea781ccba65c61c1f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9d8e381b1c634aa3f815714bee7705033e2413da` — the merge of head `5ec1a172638303071ad68d399d21e0f3b2c9ed07` into base `fa1fb6f4e0b162f768c340ea781ccba65c61c1f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9d8e381b1c634aa3f815714bee7705033e2413da && git checkout 9d8e381b1c634aa3f815714bee7705033e2413da
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa1fb6f4e0b162f768c340ea781ccba65c61c1f7 5ec1a172638303071ad68d399d21e0f3b2c9ed07 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa1fb6f4e0b162f768c340ea781ccba65c61c1f7 && git merge --no-ff 5ec1a172638303071ad68d399d21e0f3b2c9ed07

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa1fb6f4e0b162f768c340ea781ccba65c61c1f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `36887238745b5f9f82fed30f0cd27c29b8c07c79`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts + none

PR #34119 for card #34008. Read: the card body and its four comments (os-dev-report 6900296801 included), the PR body and file list (9 files, +37 / -19), the net diff from merge-base `27c2f1ea` to the head, and the head's check-runs. No file in the diff implements or enforces the three `hits`; the code they describe (plugin-auth route mounting, the admin plugin wiring, the `features.admin` and `authFamilies` producers) is outside the diff and was read on `origin/main`, not reviewed. The changeset was read for ② only; it and the five `content/docs/**` files are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Gate verdicts on this head (45 check-runs): 14 completed `success` (Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, the two shard planners, Auto Label, filter), 9 `skipped` (opt-in, schedule or queue-only jobs), none failed. IN PROGRESS at the time of this record, 22 runs: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint; CI, release and engine gates; docs and code guards; repo and tooling gates; scoped query-options erasure; scoped slot lookup and corpus). This verdict does not stand in for any of them: it judges the contract, and the merge still waits on those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets: none moves. Right. All three `hits` hunks change only a `.describe()` string literal or a JSDoc block. `AuthFamiliesSchema.admin` stays `z.boolean()`, `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema.admin` stays `z.boolean().optional()`, `AuthPluginConfigSchema.admin` stays `z.boolean().optional()`. No key, type, default, optionality or refinement is touched.
- Public surface: the published change is description text only, which reaches the generated JSON-schema descriptions and four regenerated reference pages. Right, and the diff carries those four pages.
- The docs example swap (`ban_user` to `impersonate_user` under `requiresFeature: admin`) is right against the tree: `sys_user.impersonate_user` declares `requiresFeature: 'admin'` on main, `ban_user` / `unban_user` declare none, and `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin.gatedInputs` books `create_user`, `unlock_user`, `set_user_password`, `impersonate_user` and not the ban pair.
- The dev's judgment that no test or skills follow-up is owed is right: prose only, and the report's `skills/` grep is empty.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` matches what the diff publishes: description text, no accept or refuse outcome changed. The changeset says so in its last sentence.
- `Clause-②: no` is right on the PR body, the changeset and the claim: no consumer has to change anything.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no protocol shape, key or version moves; `authFamilies` keeps its shape.
- The changeset's three bullets match the three hunks. Its second bullet ("banning and unbanning no longer appear among the operations that need the plugin") is accurate to the describe.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, file surface: the claim names `discovery.zod.ts` (`AuthFamiliesSchema.admin` describe only) and `content/docs/**`; the diff also edits `auth-endpoints.zod.ts` and `auth-config.zod.ts`. Answered, accepted. Both carry the same stale sentence the card is about, both edits are describe/JSDoc only, both are published-schema files and so are reviewed here at tier, and the changeset names them. Leaving them would have left `features.admin` and `plugins.admin` contradicting the corrected discovery text. The claim's File surface line was not amended to name them; the seat should note that on the card, it is not a contract defect.
- Deviation, no skills follow-up: answered, accepted (empty grep, see ①).
- Out of scope, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:312` comment "Platform admin: ban/unban, set-password, impersonate, set-role.": answered. Read on main; it is an internal code comment beside the plugin registration, loose and not published. Not owed by this PR. It belongs with the follow-up in S1.
- Out of scope, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` item title: answered. It makes no plugin claim; nothing owed.
- Gates: the report's one NOT MEASURED gate (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`) and its two first-run reds are left to CI; the matching CI runs are among those in progress above.
- Nothing escalated to the maintainer.

### ④ Design judgment

Route by route on `origin/main`, with `features.admin` false (better-auth admin plugin not mounted):

- Plain 404 (vendor routes that exist only on the plugin): `list-users`, `set-role`, `update-user`, `get-user`, `list-user-sessions`, `revoke-user-session`, `revoke-user-sessions`, `stop-impersonating`, and `impersonate-user`. `impersonate-user` is not a raw mount: `admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts` replaces it on the admin plugin's own `endpoints` record inside `if (enabled.admin)` (`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`), so it exists only with the plugin and is admin-gated.
- Always mounted and working (raw mounts in `auth-plugin.ts`, platform-admin gated): `ban-user`, `unban-user` (engine ban writer when `isAdminPluginMounted()` is false), `unlock-user`, `set-user-manager`, `set-user-password`, `add-sso-user`, `import-sso-users`.
- Always mounted, refusing without the plugin: `create-user` and `import-users` answer `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; `remove-user` and `has-permission` run their own gate and then hand to the vendor.

`packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts`: holds. Every example member of the family (`list-users`, `set-role`, `update-user`, `impersonate-user`) is a vendor route that 404s with the flag false. "ban-user and unban-user are not in the family: they are ObjectStack mounts, served whatever this says" is true. "Same value as features.admin ... read from the same source" is unchanged and still true (`readAuthFamilies` reads the auth service's public config). No route misclassified.

`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`: holds as a statement about the console. "The console shows those actions only when it is true" matches the four booked `gatedInputs` exactly, and "Banning and unbanning do not need it and are offered either way" matches the ungated ban pair. See S1 for what the sentence implies about `unlock-user` and `set-user-password` at the server.

`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`: the ban sentences are true. The rest is where the text can be broken; see S1 and N1.

`features.admin`, `plugins.admin` and `authFamilies.admin` now agree with each other on ban and unban, and with `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` on main.

S1 (should-fix) — `set-user-password` is still classified as an admin-plugin operation, and the new wording sharpens that. `auth-config.zod.ts` now reads "Enable platform admin operations (set-password, impersonate, set-role; ban/unban are served without it)", its JSDoc keeps "Enable better-auth's admin plugin so platform admins can set a user's password" and keeps `POST /admin/set-user-password` first in "Endpoints exposed under the auth route". On main that route is a raw mount registered unconditionally (`auth-plugin.ts`, the same block as ban-user), and its handler (`runAdminSetUserPassword` in `admin-user-endpoints.ts`) reads no admin-plugin API: it uses the core `internalAdapter`, the password hasher and the data engine, with no `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` arm of the kind `create-user` has. So, as read, it is served with the plugin off, like ban-user. Naming ban/unban as the routes served without the plugin, beside a list that still holds set-password, tells a reader the opposite. The same applies, more weakly, to "unlocking" and "setting their passwords" in the `features.admin` describe (`unlock-user` is also an unconditional mount with no plugin dependency), though that sentence is true of what the console shows. This is not a must-fix: the claim predates this PR, the card's scope is ban and unban, every sentence the PR adds is true, and the console does gate Set Password on the flag, so "enable ... operations" is true at the product level. Not driven live here (read-only), so the fix should start with a measurement: `set-user-password` and `unlock-user` with `plugins.admin` off. Either reword in this PR (say the plugin turns the console's Create / Unlock / Set Password / Impersonate actions on, and that the vendor routes are the ones that 404), or file a card carrying that measurement; the `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:312` comment, the `sys-user.object.ts` block header ("buttons that 404") and the "requires plugins.admin" heading in `authentication.mdx` go with it.

N1 (nit) — `auth-config.zod.ts` JSDoc, untouched lines: "Only callers whose user has a platform admin role (default: admin) can hit these endpoints; better-auth enforces this internally" is not true of `impersonate-user`, `create-user` or `remove-user`, which ObjectStack authorizes on the ADR-0068 platform-admin gate; and "assign global platform roles" names `set-role`, which on main still authorizes on the legacy role scalar and refuses ADR-0068 platform admins. Pre-existing, outside the card; fold into the S1 follow-up.

N2 (nit) — the discovery describe says the family's routes answer 404 and names ban/unban as the exception. Other ObjectStack `/admin/*` mounts (`unlock-user`, `set-user-password`, `create-user` with its 501) are also not in the family. The text does not claim otherwise, and the "…" covers the vendor list; no change needed.

Security: no `hits` path is under `skills/**`. No sentence this diff adds promises that an auth route is mounted, gated or refused differently from the live tree: the added sentences say ban-user and unban-user are served with the plugin off, which is what main does, and that impersonate-user belongs to the 404 family, which is what main does. Nothing in the diff changes who may call any route; every route named stays platform-admin gated. The one place the published text still under-states what is served (set-user-password, S1) errs toward telling a reader a route is absent when it is present and gated, so it opens nothing.

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `97b9f14c9d8392439a2202160308a128521d0063`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts + none

Round 2, a delta review. It continues the round-1 record on head `36887238` (PR comment 6900367724) and replaces it for this head. PR #34119, card #34008.

Read: the delta `36887238..97b9f14c`, the net diff against main, the rewritten PR body, the card's new comment (claim 6900380818), and the head's check-runs. The delta is ONE commit by the dev, parent `36887238`; the head carries no merge of main and the merge-base is still `27c2f1ea`. It touches 5 files (+27 / -21): two `hits` (`auth-endpoints.zod.ts`, `auth-config.zod.ts`), their two regenerated reference pages and the changeset. `discovery.zod.ts` is unchanged since round 1. The dev's probe table in the PR body is not in the tree and was not used: every sentence below was checked by reading `origin/main`.

Gate verdicts on this head (72 check-runs): 57 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 1 in progress (a second `Check Changeset` run; the first succeeded), and 2 FAILED: `Test Core (7/8)` and its roll-up `Test Core`. The failing test is `@objectstack/scenarios` `test/runner/run-date.test.ts`, "run on 2028-03-31", `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` (it ran 5727 ms); 33 of that package's 34 files passed. The delta touches nothing under `packages/qa`, and a describe string cannot move that test, so by reading this is a timing failure and not this diff. That is a reading, not a gate verdict: the gate is red on this head, this record does not stand in for it, and the PR does not land until that job is rerun green.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets: none moves. Right. The delta changes two `.describe()` string literals and one JSDoc block. `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema.admin` and `AuthPluginConfigSchema.admin` are still `z.boolean().optional()`.
- Public surface: description text only, with the two matching reference pages regenerated. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` still matches. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are still right on the PR body and the changeset.
- The changeset was rewritten with the delta and matches it: the title and lead now name ban, unban, unlock and set-password, and the `features.admin` and `plugins.admin` bullets say what the two describes now say. Its last sentence ("Nothing a schema accepts or refuses changes") holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- File surface: answered. The claim was re-issued (card comment 6900380818) and now names all three schema files, describe/JSDoc only. The round-1 note is closed.
- Scope beyond the card: the card names ban and unban; the delta also corrects unlock and set-password. Answered, accepted: it is the fix S1 asked for, in the same sentences, and the changeset names it.
- The two out-of-scope notes stand as answered in round 1. `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:312` and the `sys-user.object.ts` block header ("buttons that 404") and the "requires `plugins.admin`" heading in `authentication.mdx` still carry the old view of unlock and set-password; they are outside this diff and owed to a follow-up card, not to this PR.
- The dev's fix report is in the card thread, not on GitHub, and was not an input here.
- Nothing escalated to the maintainer.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts`: unchanged; the round-1 judgment holds.

`packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts`: holds. "Creating and impersonating users is available" with the plugin: `create-user` answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` when `authApi.createUser` is absent, and `impersonate-user` exists only on the admin plugin's own endpoints record. "Banning, unbanning, unlocking and setting a password answer without it": all four are raw mounts in `auth-plugin.ts` registered with no plugin condition; `unlock-user` calls `AuthManager.unlockUser` (data engine), `set-user-password` uses the core `internalAdapter` and password hasher, and neither reads an admin-plugin API. "The console still shows its unlock and set-password actions only when it is true" matches `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin.gatedInputs` (`create_user`, `unlock_user`, `set_user_password`, `impersonate_user`) and the four `requiresFeature: 'admin'` declarations on `sys_user`.

`packages/spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts`: the split is right route by route. Needs the plugin: `create-user` (501 without), `impersonate-user`, `stop-impersonating`, `set-role`, `list-users`, `list-user-sessions`, `revoke-user-session(s)` (vendor routes, absent without the plugin), and `remove-user` (an ObjectStack mount that runs the gate and then hands to the vendor route). Served either way: `ban-user`, `unban-user`, `unlock-user`, `set-user-password`. The describe follows the same split. One new sentence does not hold; see S2.

The three descriptions now agree with each other and with the tree on which operations the plugin turns on.

S1 — CLOSED. `set-user-password` and `unlock-user` are no longer described as needing the plugin in either file, and the `features.admin` describe keeps the true console statement apart from the server one. Closed on the tree reading above, not on the probe numbers.

N1 — CLOSED in part. "Assign global platform roles" is gone and "better-auth enforces this internally" is replaced by a sentence that names which doors run the ADR-0068 gate and which keep the vendor's role-scalar check. That replacement is right for every route it names, and wrong for one it covers without naming: S2.

S2 (should-fix) — new in this delta. The JSDoc now says "Every one of these doors is platform-admin gated", then sorts them into two groups: the ObjectStack mounts, `create-user`, `remove-user` and `impersonate-user` on the ADR-0068 gate, and "the vendor routes left as better-auth ships them (`set-role`, `list-users`, …)" on the legacy `user.role` check. `POST /admin/stop-impersonating` is in the endpoint list six lines above and fits neither group. On main it is a vendor route left as shipped, it is carried by the IMPERSONATED user's session, and it is authorized by the signed `admin_session` cookie alone, with no admin check of the caller (`auth-manager-request-routing.ts` at the #8243 block, `impersonation-bearer-rotation.ts`, and `admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts`, which classifies it as "the EXIT from an impersonation ... carried by the impersonated session"). So the sentence promises a gate the route does not run. Not a must-fix: the route is not open (the cookie is minted only by the gated impersonate door), nothing a consumer builds changes, and it is JSDoc, not the published describe. Fix by excepting it in that sentence, for example: `stop-impersonating` is the exit from an impersonation, carried by the impersonated session and authorized by its `admin_session` cookie.

N2 (nit) — unchanged from round 1; no change needed.

N3 (nit) — `auth-config.zod.ts` JSDoc lists `POST /admin/list-users`; on main the route is `GET` (`vendor-admin-refusal-envelope.ts`, and the dogfood pin reads `GET /auth/admin/list-users`). An untouched line; fix it with S2.

N4 (nit) — the tree pins ban and unban with the plugin off (`pending-sso-users.test.ts`). Nothing committed pins `unlock-user` or `set-user-password` with it off; the dev's probe was thrown away. The prose is right today by reading, with no test to turn red if it stops being right. Worth a line on the follow-up card.

N5 (nit) — "ObjectStack mounts that write through the platform" is loose: with the plugin on, ban-user writes through better-auth's `internalAdapter`, and set-user-password does in both states. "Served with the plugin off as well as on" is the true part and is enough.

Security: no `hits` path is under `skills/**`. The delta's sentences about which routes are mounted and which are served without the plugin match the live tree. One sentence promises gating the tree does not have: S2, `stop-impersonating` described as platform-admin gated. It over-states a check on an exit route that is still held by a signed credential, so it opens nothing. No other sentence says a route is mounted, gated or refused differently from main.

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Round 3, a delta review. It continues the round-2 record on head `97b9f14c` (PR comment 6900983847) and replaces it for this head. PR #34119, card #34008.

### ① Derived judgments

### ③ Boundary flags

- Still owed to a follow-up card, outside this diff, unchanged from round 2: the stale view of unlock and set-password in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts:312`, the `sys-user.object.ts` block header and the "requires `plugins.admin`" heading in `authentication.mdx`, plus N4 below.
